output.brief:
The slowdown isn't mainly Corvane, the new hires, or the valuation firm. It comes from one policy change. Credit Policy v14 (effective 1 May, clause 6.3) now requires a full inspection appraisal for property collateral above $150k. The old threshold was $500k. Full appraisals went from about 30 a month to about 80. They take about 8.6 days, against about 1.2 for desktop valuations. The valuation firm's turnaround per type hasn't changed. Property-secured loans went from 1.6 to 8.4 days at the valuation stage. Unsecured loans, which are on the same Corvane system and the same branches, are back to about 5.9 days. Document collection at the new-hire branches matches the other branches. Underwriting time is flat, so Hub capacity isn't the cause. The policy's impact on processing times was "not assessed", and the audit finding that prompted the change is a real risk reason.
Recommendation: don't withhold Corvane's payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay to the credit risk committee alongside the audit rationale, so it can decide whether to keep, tier or speed up the rule. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Withdrawals are partly an artefact of the 30-day auto-close rule, so check them separately before launching any fee rebate. Confidence is high on the cause and moderate on the withdrawals.
